newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe hospitals closed; arrested doctors freed.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe hospitals closed; arrested doctors freed.

text.p: Zimbabwe's two main hospitals closed their doors to patients on Wednesday after junior doctors and other medical staff went on strike to protest against the arrest of two colleagues.
Doctors Farai Jiah and Austin Bene -- leaders of the state Hospitals Doctors Association who had been arrested on charges of inciting a strike by nurses -- were later freed by a Harare magistrate.
The magistrate said he needed time to decide whether to refer their case to the Supreme Court, as their lawyer had raised constitutional issues during an initial remand hearing.
Union officials were unavailable for comment on whether the strike, which closed the capital's main hospitals, would continue.
Authorities at Parirenyatwa and Harare hospitals met government officials to discuss the crisis.

"We have made our recommendations to government on what we think should be done with the current situation. We only hope and pray that the situation will be resolved soon because we are in a very difficult position," Harare Hospital superintendent Yasin Ali told reporters.
Earlier a doctor at the hospital, the capital's largest, said the situation was "chaotic" and new patients were being turned away: "The whole health system is in shambles."

Callistus Madziwa, medical superintendent at Parirenyatwa Hospital, said: "We are turning away all new cases now because there is nobody here to care for patients and all critically ill patients will be discharged."
He said the hospital was asking relatives to take critically ill patients and care for them at home. Surgeons were refering emergency cases to private clinics.
Acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said he would meet union officials on Thursday to discuss the strike.

Junior doctors, theatre staff and physiotherapists walked out on Tuesday because of Jiah and Bene's arrest. They were charged with inciting nurses to go on strike on October 21 to back demands for higher pay, allowances and negotiations on working conditions.
The government reacted to the nurses' strike by firing the estimated 10,000 nurses last week. The junior doctors, who had gone on strike with the nurses, returned to work a week ago.
